title: Shape and edges of an encoded path instance
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a Boolean-valued relation on the indices $0,1,\ldots,n-1$, and let $s,t$ be such indices. If a bit string $x$ is the nested self-delimiting encoding of the unary string of $n$ true bits, the row-major list of entries of $A$, and the binary expansions of $s$ and $t$, then $x$ has the prescribed unary, matrix, and endpoint shape for $n,s,t$. Moreover, for every pair of indices $u,v<n$, the encoded path relation holds exactly when $A(u,v)$ is true.
hypotheses_covered: x equals the encoding of n, A, s, and t
